title: The Best Mewtwo Cards to Collect — Base Set to Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex, Raw to PSA 10, Dated Sold Prices | Gengar's Collector's Desk
description: Gengar's pick of the Mewtwo cards that are true collectibles: Base Set Mewtwo (1st Edition, Shadowless, Unlimited), Shining Mewtwo from Neo Destiny, Mewtwo VSTAR from the Crown Zenith gallery, the Hidden Fates shiny, Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex from Destined Rivals and Ascended Heroes, the 30th Celebration Mewtwos and an under-$20 shelf — each with dated raw, PSA 9, PSA 10 and TAG 10 sold prices and eBay links.
keywords: best mewtwo cards, mewtwo cards to collect, base set mewtwo, shining mewtwo, team rocket's mewtwo ex, mewtwo vstar crown zenith, most valuable mewtwo cards, mewtwo card collection
intro: Mewtwo was the first Pokémon that felt dangerous, and the card game has treated it that way for 27 years: a Base Set holo, the Shining, the Rocket version, and now a Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex that is the heaviest card in its set. These are the ones I'd keep, from a $3 holo to a Shadowless slab.
narratorNote: Mewtwo and I have a history — a ghost and a psychic type do not get along in the games. In the binder it's a different story. Every number here is a dated sold price from our own index data, every print is searched by its exact set and number, and nothing on this desk is a call to buy or sell.

shelves.label: The grails
shelves.blurb: The two Wizards-era Mewtwo holos that define the character's collection, each in its separate prints.

entries.title: Base Set Mewtwo #10 (1999)
entries.why: The Base Set holo, the card that put Mewtwo on the kitchen table in 1999. Like every Base Set holo it is three separate cards — 1st Edition, Shadowless and Unlimited — with separate PSA labels and separate prices, and the Unlimited raw copy is still cheap enough that a collector can own the art for the price of lunch while deciding which lane to chase graded.

entries.title: Shining Mewtwo, Neo Destiny #109 (2002)
entries.why: A secret-rare Shining from the last Neo set, with the foil on the Pokémon instead of the background. The Shining Charizard gets the headlines; the Shining Mewtwo is the one that still looks like a secret. The 1st Edition is the serious print, and its PSA 10 almost never comes to market, which is why the ladder shows a single dated sale rather than a mark.

shelves.label: The centerpieces
shelves.blurb: Modern Mewtwos with a clear chase slot and a graded market deep enough to mark every week.

entries.title: Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex, Destined Rivals (2025)
entries.why: Destined Rivals brought Team Rocket back and this Mewtwo is the set's heaviest card in our index. The Special Illustration Rare #231 is the chase; the gold #240 is the hyper-rare frame. The regular-art #213 is on the starter shelf below.

entries.title: Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex #281, Ascended Heroes (2026)
entries.why: The 2026 follow-up in Ascended Heroes, where a second Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex Special Illustration Rare landed among the set's top weights. A pair with the Destined Rivals card for anyone building the Rocket run.

entries.title: Mewtwo VSTAR GG44, Crown Zenith (2023)
entries.why: From the Crown Zenith Galarian Gallery, the illustration-rare subset that closed out Sword & Shield. The gallery Mewtwo VSTAR is one of the heaviest cards in our Crown Zenith index and the most-wanted Mewtwo of its era.

entries.title: Mewtwo GX SV59, Hidden Fates (2019)
entries.why: The shiny full art from the Hidden Fates Shiny Vault. Sits in the same vault as the Charizard GX SV49 and the Umbreon GX SV69 and has aged the same way.

entries.title: Mewtwo ex, 30th Celebration (2026)
entries.why: The 30th Celebration set printed Mewtwo ex twice at the top end, #151 and #157. Both are too new for graded marks that meet our rule, so the ladder shows the raw mark and stays quiet on the rest.

shelves.label: The starter shelf
shelves.blurb: Mewtwos for under $20 raw. Each one is a real card from a real set and the first Mewtwo somebody pulled.

entries.title: Mewtwo EX #54, Celebrations (2021)
entries.why: The Classic Collection reprint of the Next Destinies Mewtwo EX, with the Celebrations gold stamp. A real 2012-era chase card's art for a few dollars.

entries.title: Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex #213, Destined Rivals (2025)
entries.why: The regular-art print of the Destined Rivals Mewtwo. Same card, same set, a fraction of the SIR price.

entries.title: Mewtwo GX #31, Hidden Fates (2019)
entries.why: The main-set Mewtwo GX from Hidden Fates, the affordable cousin of the SV59 shiny above.

entries.title: Mewtwo #150, Scarlet & Violet 151 (2023)
entries.why: The 151 set's Mewtwo, numbered by Pokédex. A few dollars raw, and the Pokédex numbering is half the fun of that set.

entries.title: Mewtwo #59, Crown Zenith (2023)
entries.why: The regular Crown Zenith Mewtwo. Pairs with the GG44 above for a two-card set from the same box.

collectingNotes.p: 1st Edition, Shadowless and Unlimited are three separate assets with separate PSA labels, separate population reports and separate price histories. Our indices track each print as its own card and every link on this page searches for the exact print on its row.

collectingNotes.h: Two Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex cards
collectingNotes.p: Destined Rivals (2025) and Ascended Heroes (2026) each have a Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex Special Illustration Rare. They are different cards with different numbers, and a search that drops the set name will mix them.

On modern Special Illustration Rares a PSA 9 sells for about what the raw card does; the premium is almost entirely in the PSA 10. On the vintage holos the gap is far wider, and a raw vintage mark is a typical raw sale in any condition, not a near-mint price.

PSA 10 is the hobby's price reference. TAG grades by machine-measured imaging with human review and publishes a full defect report for every card, which is why we link TAG slabs beside PSA on every row. We think measured grading is where the hobby is heading — our view, not a price claim. How TAG grading works →
